A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 25 readable pages, including Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original training and evaluation of 50 language models, including downstream scores, data-repetition experiments, validation curves, and supplementary evaluation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices G–L, including comparisons of dual-objective and single-objective models.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same weighted autoregressive/masked-diffusion objective, masked next-token prediction, shared transformer, and training procedure. The loss-formulation erratum in Appendix B was already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English HPLT v2 training data, nine downstream benchmarks in Table 1, data-repetition scenarios, and autoregressive, bidirectional, and prefix evaluations.

E2.justification: The autoregressive-only and masked-diffusion-only comparators remain unchanged, as does the PLL versus Monte Carlo comparison. Table 11 replaces the masked-diffusion label 0:1 with the equivalent α = 0; this is the same comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain 470M-parameter models trained on 32B tokens, the same repetition configurations, evaluation splits, zero-shot protocols, score normalization, and PLL mask selection. Table 8 converts percentages to equivalent α fractions without changing settings.

E4.justification: The objective-weight/repetition study, prefix-generalization analysis, validation curves in Appendix G, mask-count sensitivity in Appendix H, and evaluation-method comparison in Appendix J are unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same Gaussian-process noise model and posterior sampling for estimating optimal-α distributions. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported scores, rankings, and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains average autoregressive scores of 19.1 for dual-objective training and 9.4 for autoregressive-only training at 128 repetitions.

T1.justification: The equations, Appendix B loss-formulation erratum, and Appendix F definitions, left-shift closure theorem, constructive proof, and corollary are identical in substance. None is newly introduced in v3.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about combining training efficiency with overfitting resistance, optimal objective balance, and induced prefix capability. The shortened introductory wording does not change their scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of regular-data versus data-constrained behavior, hypotheses about larger-model generalization, validation-noise caveat, and interpretations of mask-count effects. No substantive limitation or qualification changes.

D1.justification: Architecture, optimization, tokenizer, evaluation implementation, GPU resources, training-time estimates, and code/model release information are unchanged. The author affiliation and contact edits do not alter reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 6 remain unchanged. Capitalization edits to several reference titles concern the same publications and do not add or remove related work.

P1.justification: v3 shortens an introductory paragraph and Figure 1's caption, updates author information, adds a front-page equal-contribution footnote, and standardizes table terminology and reference capitalization. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds conference headers, reformats the author block, slightly repositions Figure 1, and adjusts labels, alignment, or spacing in Tables 8, 9, and 11. No figures or tables are added or removed, and the plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 mainly updates publication and author formatting and makes small notation and table-presentation refinements. These edits leave the method, empirical evidence, theory, interpretations, and reproducibility information unchanged across the main text and appendices, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
